_comment: PLAT-37 — THE VISION TIER'S THRESHOLDS.
THIS FILE HOLDS THE WINNERS. THE LOSERS ARE A PROGRAM, NOT A TABLE HERE.
Verification-Harness-Traps §36b: 'the winner is gated, the losers are
prose' — a harness that picks one parameter out of several and records
'I measured the others and they were vacuous' asserts the winner and
writes the losers in a comment, which nothing ever re-takes and which is
therefore free to be wrong. PLAT-30 published a three-row table in three
documents and every figure about a pair that was NOT committed was wrong.
So the rejected candidates are re-derivable in a minute:
just plat37-threshold-probe
which sweeps every candidate over whatever frames are in build/plat37 and
reports, for each, how many real frames clear it AND how many BLANK
CONTROLS clear it. A candidate both sides clear is not a weak threshold;
it is not a threshold.
EVERY ONE OF THESE IS A COMPARISON AGAINST A BLANK CONTROL CAPTURED IN
THE SAME RUN, ON THE SAME COMPOSITOR, WITH NO CLIENT ATTACHED. That is
PLAT-37's rule 2 and it is not decoration: an absolute similarity
threshold with no blank beside it is a number nobody can falsify (§7b),
and a 'not blank' check with no blank to compare against is §4.
isonim-gpui/scripts/wayland-capture-frame.sh retains that frame at
<out>.blank and FAILS when it cannot take one — before PLAT-37 it
observed the blank screen and threw the frame away, and printed
'continuing anyway' when the screen never blanked.
THE RATCHET RULE, INHERITED FROM PLAT-35's thresholds.json AND FROM
Methodologies/visual-design-iteration.md: a threshold LOOSENED TWICE is a
defect in the CAPTURE, not in the threshold. Each entry carries its own
history and the gate fails on a second loosening. 'Loosening' has a
direction per entry and it is stated on the entry, because two of these
are floors and one is a ceiling and a single spelling of 'raised' would
be wrong for one of them.
WHY TWO IMAGE METRICS AND NOT ONE. SSIM alone can be moved by a uniform
luminance shift — a frame that is merely a different shade of nothing
would score low against a black screen while containing no structure at
all. edgeChangeRatio asks the second question: does the frame have EDGES
the control does not. A flat fill clears the first and fails the second,
and only the pair can tell that from a drawn screen.
ALL FIGURES BELOW WERE TAKEN ON ONE HOST AND THE HOST IS RECORDED IN
build/plat37/manifest.json's `host` block AND in
src/tests/visual/plat37-measurements.json's `provenance`, INCLUDING the
resolved ffmpeg and tesseract versions. GuiAssert's flake pins nixpkgs
b6018f87 and names no version string for either binary, so an OCR or SSIM
figure without them beside it is a §28 coin flip.

maxSsimVsBlank.why: computeSsim(frame, blankControl) must be BELOW this. A window that opened and painted nothing scores 1.0 against the blank control, which is exactly the pass-shaped failure the windowed lane exists to see. THE SWEEP ADMITTED EVERY CANDIDATE FROM 0.10 TO 0.99 — the six frames score 0.0004 to 0.0008 and the control scores exactly 1.0, so the separation is three orders of magnitude and the choice within the admitted range is nearly free. The TIGHTEST admitted candidate is committed rather than a comfortable one, because a ceiling with slack under it is a budget for a frame that is half blank.

history.change: introduced, by hand, before the sweep existed
TIGHTENED to the tightest candidate the sweep admits

minEdgeChangeRatioVsBlank.why: edgeChangeRatio(blankControl, frame) must be ABOVE this, so the frame has STRUCTURE and not merely luminance. The blank control against itself scores 0.0 by construction, which is the falsification. WHAT THIS QUANTITY ACTUALLY SAYS, said plainly because the number looks stronger than it is: GuiAssert computes |edges(a) XOR edges(b)| / |edges(a) OR edges(b)|, and the blank control has NO edge pixels at all, so every captured frame scores EXACTLY 1.0 and the sweep admitted every candidate from 0.0005 to 0.20. Against an edge-free control the metric SATURATES, and the real content of this floor is 'the frame has edge pixels at all'. That is still a claim SSIM cannot make — a uniform fill scores low on SSIM and zero here — but it is not a graded measure of structure, and reading it as one would be the error. The tightest admitted candidate is committed.

history.change: introduced, by hand, before the sweep existed
TIGHTENED to the tightest candidate the sweep admits

_comment: THE JOIN'S PARAMETERS, AND THE ONE PUBLISHED CONTROL THAT COULD NOT BE
MADE TO LAND.
PLAT-37 publishes the join as: of the K longest strings introspection
reports for that scenario, at least M appear in the frame's OCR, with
two negative controls — the blank frame scores zero, and ANOTHER
SCENARIO'S FRAME SCORES LOWER THAN ITS OWN.
THE SECOND CONTROL CANNOT HOLD ON THIS CORPUS. Measured by the probe
over every needle-length window and over two selectors: at the
committed window the per-scenario own:away pairs are 3:3 3:3 5:5 3:2
5:6 3:3, and there is no window in which every scenario scores
strictly better at home. The cause is the corpus rather than the
metric — all six scenarios open the SAME recording and draw the SAME
source into the same editor, so the strings OCR can read are very
largely shared. `distinctiveNeedles` finds text NO other scenario
draws for only three of the six, and none at all for stepped-editor
and breakpoint-editor, which differ by a gutter MARK rather than by
text. That is Verification-Harness-Traps §34 — the population, not the
property.
§36's rule for a published control that cannot land is that the repair
goes to the ASSERTION or to the DESIGN and never to the measurement.
So the control's PURPOSE — catching a normalisation loose enough to
match anything — is carried by two controls that DO land, and the
cross-scenario number is still computed and RECORDED per scenario as
the evidence for this paragraph:
the BLANK frame     zero hits, every scenario.
the EDIT-MODE frame zero hits, every scenario, against own scores of
3 to 5. `ct edit --ui=gpui src/frontend/gpui`
is the same binary in the same run with the same
pane chrome, drawing this front-end's own working
tree instead of the calc recording — the one
screen in the capture whose TEXT is different.
THE NEEDLE WINDOW IS A SWEPT PARAMETER AND THE FIRST VALUE WAS WRONG.
`planNeedles` originally took the K longest strings with no ceiling,
and on the real corpus that scored 0 or 1 hits out of K=10 on every
scenario — a join red everywhere, which measures nothing. The longest
text nodes this front-end draws are whole source lines and docstring
paragraphs of 58 to 63 normalised characters; a needle is matched as a
contiguous substring, so one misread glyph in sixty kills it, and the
panes clip so many are not on screen to be read at all.

crossScenarioControl.why: measured and recorded per scenario; it cannot land on this corpus and the reason is the corpus. See the comment above. Gating it would gate a property of a scenario set this milestone does not own.

minHitRatio.why: Of the K longest distinct normalised strings the render plan carries for THAT scenario, within the 8..24 character window, at least this fraction must be legible in concatenatedText(runOcr(frame)). K is derived from the plan and never from a list — a hand-written list of expected strings is a fixture, and a fixture is satisfied by a front-end that draws the fixture. K is asserted non-zero AND at or above minK: a join whose K is zero is satisfied by any frame, which is §4 arriving through an empty numerator. The committed value is the worst own ratio the sweep measured at the committed window (3 of 10), taken without slack for the same reason the two image thresholds are taken at their tightest.

history.change: introduced, by hand, before the sweep existed
LOWERED to the worst ratio the corpus actually scores; the 0.4 was a guess that no scenario met
